subsystems.name: Bacterial spores
subsystems.role: dormant life that wakes when water enters a crack and starts producing limestone.
parts: protective carrier (expanded clay, hydrogel, or microcapsule)

subsystems.name: Nutrient source
subsystems.role: food the bacteria metabolise to make calcium carbonate.
parts: yeast extract or other organic co-nutrients

subsystems.name: Concrete matrix
subsystems.role: the structural material that carries load and hosts the healing agents.

subsystems.name: Activation mechanism
subsystems.role: water and oxygen entering a crack trigger germination and healing.

subsystems.name: Healing product
subsystems.role: calcium carbonate crystals that fill the crack and block further water flow.

buildSteps.title: Select the bacteria
buildSteps.detail: Choose spore-forming strains that survive the high pH of fresh concrete and can lie dormant for years.

buildSteps.title: Encapsulate the spores
buildSteps.detail: Spores are immobilised in expanded clay pellets, hydrogel beads or microcapsules so the alkaline pore water does not kill them.

buildSteps.title: Prepare the nutrient
buildSteps.detail: Calcium lactate (and sometimes yeast extract) is dried and either mixed as a powder or sealed in separate capsules.

buildSteps.title: Batch the concrete
buildSteps.detail: Encapsulated spores and nutrient are added during mixing, replacing a small fraction of the fine aggregate.

buildSteps.title: Cast and cure
buildSteps.detail: The concrete is placed and cured normally; the spores stay dormant as long as the concrete is dry.

buildSteps.title: Crack forms and water enters
buildSteps.detail: When the concrete cracks and water seeps in, the capsules break or swell, releasing spores and nutrient.

buildSteps.title: Germination and metabolism
buildSteps.detail: Spores germinate; the bacteria consume calcium lactate and produce calcium carbonate as a by-product.

buildSteps.title: Precipitation heals the crack
buildSteps.detail: Calcite crystals grow to fill the crack, typically up to about 0.8 mm wide, sealing it against further water ingress.

prerequisites.why: strains that survive concrete's pH above 12 are known and cultured in labs.
carriers must protect spores during batching yet release them when a crack opens.

prerequisites.tech: Nutrient that does not weaken concrete
prerequisites.why: added organics can retard setting or reduce strength if dosed poorly.
decades of dormancy and repeated healing cycles are not yet proven in the field.

pathway.milestone: lab and pilot projects, with a small number of commercial products mainly in Europe
pathway.unlocks: proof that cracks can self-seal in real elements.

pathway.milestone: field trials in bridges, tunnels, retaining walls and marine structures
pathway.unlocks: data on durability, healing repeatability and cost.

pathway.milestone: standardised mix designs and testing methods
pathway.unlocks: specifiers can call for self-healing concrete with confidence.
longer service life, less inspection and lower maintenance for concrete assets.
